subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion categorically reject every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, including empty and canonical OpenClaw checkouts?
rationale: The PR closes a real update-source trust gap but deliberately breaks the currently documented conversion behavior and requires operator action, so the permanent security-versus-compatibility policy needs owner intent.

options.title: Approve fresh-only conversion
options.body: Keep categorical refusal as the security invariant, replace sidecar recovery state with shared SQLite, and document the guided migration path.

options.title: Add explicit break-glass adoption
options.body: Preserve fresh cloning by default but allow a clearly dangerous, maintainer-approved opt-in for users who intentionally own an existing checkout.

options.title: Pause for updater redesign
options.body: Do not land the compatibility change until conversion can stage and swap a verified checkout without requiring users to manage destination paths manually.

recommendation.title: Approve fresh-only conversion
recommendation.body: Keep categorical refusal as the security invariant, replace sidecar recovery state with shared SQLite, and document the guided migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to update handoff and package-update behavior around the affected boundary.
